title: Make Ctrl+C stop a flooding pane at once and spare main's core
notes: Measured: seq flat out: main 109-112% CPU, renderer 110-119%, renderer heap 124-208 MB; 59% of main's busy time is the headless xterm copy (pane-screen-copy.ts) with no remote screen joined. Ctrl+C keeps printing 2.5-2.6 s (~9M lines). Typing beside it fine (24-27 ms). Where: src/main/main.ts:429 copy.push, no flow control from xterm's write queue to the pty. Fix (medium): feed the copy only while a host port is set or the window is away; pause the pty past a write-queue high-water mark. Rerun: measure.mjs flood shown|hidden. From profiling card dca04e6f, docs/performance/history.md 2026-11-02.

comments.body: Unconfirmed: the 2.5-2.6 s after Ctrl+C came from a run of seq 1 30000017, which could have reached its last line in that time, so it may be seq finishing rather than Ctrl+C landing late. flood now runs seq 1 inf and prints whether the pane stopped. Rerun it before sizing the pty flow-control fix on this number. See docs/performance/history.md.
Confirmed with seq 1 inf (PR #166): the pane stops, but 3.2 s after Ctrl+C.

Shipped in PR #185: main keeps a pane's screen copy only while host.port is set or the window shows another host; the renderer pauses a pane's pty past 100k queued characters (1 s lease, renewed every 0.5 s); the pane host resumes every shell when the app disconnects. Flood: main 102-115% -> 35-51%, Ctrl+C 2.6-4.4 s -> 0.11 s, with and without the pane host.
